snippet.title: Alan Rickman’s Secret “Cousins” on the Harry Potter Set
snippet.description:
💛 Alan Rickman’s “cousins” weren’t his cousins at all.

On the set of the Harry Potter films, Alan Rickman, who played Professor Snape, often had visitors he called his cousins or friends. Tom Felton, who played Draco Malfoy, revealed the secret in a tribute for The Guardian, ten years after Rickman’s death. Rickman often had about half a dozen visitors a day. They were terminally ill children and their families. 🕯️

Rickman never greeted them as himself, according to Felton. He stayed in character as Snape, sneering at them and telling them to tuck in their shirts. He understood that the children didn’t come to meet an actor. They came to meet the character they loved. ✨

Producer Paula DuPré Pesmen, who organized set visits for children, remembered one visit in particular. A teenage boy named Jay, who had stage 4 neuroblastoma, was visiting the set of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. He told her what he really wished for: to be in the film.

Rickman, in full Snape costume, turned to her and asked in Snape’s voice why that child wasn’t in the film. Everyone laughed. Then he took Jay by the hand and led him into the crowd of children in a classroom scene. Jay appeared in a shot from behind. It didn’t make the final cut, but Jay was thrilled. 🎬

There was no publicity and no fuss. Just kindness, delivered in the way each child could enjoy it most.

Alan Rickman died on January 14, 2016, at age 69. Ten years later, his co-stars are still sharing what kind of man he was. 💚
